- Alexander invaded northwest India in 326 BCE during the reign of the Nanda dynasty in Magadha, ruled at the time by Dhana Nanda (identified as Agrammes or Xandrames by classical Greek historians).
- Maurya (Option B) is incorrect because Chandragupta Maurya defeated Dhana Nanda and established the Maurya Empire only after Alexander's campaign, around 321–322 BCE.
- Sunga (Option C) is incorrect because Pushyamitra Sunga founded this dynasty around 185 BCE after assassinating the last Mauryan ruler, Brihadratha, over 140 years after Alexander's invasion.
- Kanva (Option D) is incorrect because Vasudeva Kanva established the Kanva dynasty around 73 BCE by deposing the last Sunga king, Devabhuti, centuries after Alexander.
- Often confused with: The Maurya dynasty, because Chandragupta Maurya famously fought Alexander's general, Seleucus I Nicator (c. 305 BCE), leading candidates to mistakenly believe the Mauryas were in power during Alexander's invasion itself.
issues_found: Commonly misses the precise chronological marker of Alexander's invasion (326 BCE) versus the founding of the Maurya Empire (c. 322–321 BCE).
Candidates frequently confuse Alexander's invasion with the later Maurya-Seleucid conflict (c. 305 BCE).
